notes: The first real performance run at or above the floor, which the synthetic performance fixture was standing in for. A terminal-mode run stopped at its first mandatory gate, so phase-1 and phase-2 are done and the specification summary is still null: performance_context is populated rather than merely present (bottlenecks_identified 6, the four bottleneck_priorities counters, and phase_summaries for codebase_analysis and bottleneck_analysis carrying decision/rationale objects, risk strings and artifact entries), and verification_context is present and empty, which is what a run that has not verified anything writes. Artifacts sit at the A4 performance layout (analysis/) and each opens with the A5 summary block; all three are truncated after their first body section. dashboard-data.js is strict JSON. One thing this fixture does NOT prove, stated because its validating is luck rather than contract: the performance orchestrator's own prose tells it to write task_context.clarifications_resolved beside performance_context, and A1 freezes exactly one per-workflow context block - this run happened to record its unasked clarifications in the artifacts instead, so the collision never fired. The migration run sampled the same day obeyed the equivalent instruction and was refused by the schema, and landed only with those two lines removed by hand; the conflict is filed, not fixed here. Nothing here came from a real repository - the task is an invented local problem in a scratch project (a stocktake report that re-reads its catalogue inside a loop), so the only pseudonymization is the source alias above; no absolute path, user name or ticket id appears in the sampled bytes. Em dashes and the minus, sigma, section and middle-dot glyphs of the analysis prose were replaced with ASCII, the middle dot with * where it multiplied.
